summary:
ALLIS (Autonomous Lunar Landing Intelligence System) is an interactive web-based lunar landing analysis platform developed to address the challenges of identifying safe and suitable landing locations on the Moon. The system combines interactive 3D lunar visualisation with terrain analysis and a rule-based assessment framework to evaluate potential landing regions based on factors such as surface elevation, slope, craters, terrain irregularities and potential hazards.

Inspired by NASA's lunar exploration research, including LRO, LOLA and SPLICE technologies, ALLIS transforms complex lunar terrain concepts into accessible visual insights. Users can explore lunar environments, examine surface characteristics and compare landing-site suitability through an interactive interface.

By helping users understand potential landing hazards before a mission, ALLIS demonstrates how intelligent analysis and visualisation can support safer, more informed lunar landing decisions. It contributes to the broader goal of advancing autonomous navigation and reducing risks in future lunar exploration.
details:
ALLIS (Autonomous Lunar Landing Intelligence System) is an interactive web-based platform designed to demonstrate how technology and intelligent analysis can help identify safer landing locations on the Moon. The project addresses one of the major challenges of lunar exploration: selecting a suitable landing site while accounting for unpredictable terrain, geographical obstacles and environmental conditions.

How It Works

ALLIS provides an interactive environment where users can explore a visually represented lunar surface through 3D visualisation. The platform incorporates lunar terrain representations and a rule-based analysis framework to assess potential landing regions. It considers important factors such as surface elevation, slope steepness, craters, terrain irregularities and potential landing hazards. Based on these factors, the system presents analytical insights to help users understand the relative suitability of different landing areas.

The website also incorporates interactive visual elements, data presentation and a user-friendly interface to make complex lunar landing concepts easier to understand. Its visualisation environment helps users explore the Moon and interpret geographical information rather than relying solely on numerical data.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The primary benefit of ALLIS is its ability to demonstrate how terrain analysis and intelligent decision-support concepts can contribute to safer lunar exploration. Identifying potentially hazardous landing areas before spacecraft descent could help reduce landing risks, protect valuable equipment and support more effective mission planning. The project aims to encourage the development of autonomous landing technologies and make lunar surface analysis more accessible and understandable.

Tools and Technologies

The project was developed as a web-based application using HTML, CSS and JavaScript. JavaScript powers the interactive functionality and analytical logic, while HTML and CSS provide the website structure, visual design, animations and responsive interface. The platform incorporates interactive 3D visualisation and simulated lunar terrain to create an immersive exploration experience. Development also involved GitHub for version control and project collaboration, alongside AI-assisted development tools.

NASA's lunar exploration research, including Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) and Safe and Precise Landing – Integrated Capabilities Evolution (SPLICE), informed the project's technical concepts and research direction. The current prototype uses simulated terrain and rule-based analysis rather than directly processing live NASA datasets.

Creativity and Innovation

What makes ALLIS distinctive is its combination of scientific concepts, interactive 3D visualisation and an accessible decision-support interface. Instead of presenting lunar landing analysis as a purely technical process, the project creates an immersive digital environment in which users can explore the lunar surface and understand the factors that influence landing-site selection.

Factors Considered

During development, the team considered landing safety, terrain elevation, slope gradients, crater distribution, surface irregularities, potential hazards, visual clarity, usability and the importance of presenting analytical information in an understandable format. The project was also designed with the broader objectives of future lunar exploration and autonomous spacecraft navigation in mind.

Ultimately, ALLIS demonstrates how interactive technology and intelligent terrain assessment can contribute to the future of safer, more informed lunar exploration.
